paper.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

region.name: Siftsand
region.tagline: A snake who can't keep it all.

briefing: Right. No more easy ones. In Siftsand, a snake carries beads down an endless road.
One tiny belly, yet he never forgets a bead? HA! Bring me his secret.
You'll fail. ...I keep saying that. Why do I keep saying that? GO.
reminder: Not done? Good. GOOD. I mean... hurry up, Speck.
Read the Cursed Book. Most of a desert is just sand.
return: An hourglass. It shut out my coffee grounds and kept the sugar cube. HMPH.
Bell, Lens, hourglass... Look at those bottle caps. They're humming. Together.
That's not in any paper I know. ...Yet.

arrival: A desert post at the start of the Endless Road.
Noodle the snake carries the message beads. He also swallows all the sand.
resolution: Noodle gulps a ruby, lets the sand slide by, and grins. Belly never full.
Penny stamps a tiny parcel DELIVERED. Inside: an hourglass. 'For your giant.'

inhabitants.name: Noodle
inhabitants.role: Giver of c1. The outpost's courier, a very long green sand snake with one small belly (the fixed-size state). He gulps every grain the same way (time-invariant), so at the bell he can only say mush. Sweet, burpy, easily excited; his happy loop-de-loop after c1 pops a vertebra (sets up c2). His default only shows if a later item of his is locked (so only after c1): keep it timeless.

default: Beads to carry, bells to answer! *burp*
afterSolved: Beads in, sand out! I'm a picky eater now.
My back went *pop*. Doc Marrow fixes backs. Mostly.

inhabitants.name: Tumble
inhabitants.role: Flavour, and the region's curious kid: rides on Noodle's tail and wants to know where the road ends. Gives f1 (hidden state: already in the book in normal play, so his first talk opens with its known line, then his default, or f2 after c1) and f2 (exponential decay, after c1). afterSolved needs f2, so it only shows after c1. Never explains anything.

default: I'm Tumble! I ride on Noodle's tail. Where does the road END?
His belly gurgles in colours. Mostly the colour of sand.
afterSolved: Noodle says ruby, lapis, emerald now! Next I'm teaching him 'please'.

inhabitants.name: Kayvee
inhabitants.role: Red herring and flavour: a sandy desert pack-rat who never chooses and keeps every letter forever (attention's KV cache: no compression, so each lookup gets slower as the pile grows; Section 3.1). His overflowing letter cart is the right pan of the c2 scale (a Transformer layer's MHA + MLP). Gives f3 (Big-O, his first talk after c1: each new letter checked against every letter in his cart). Default shows before c1; afterSolved from f3 on.

default: Why choose? I keep EVERY letter. Every single one. Forever!
My cart's overflowing. Finding one letter takes longer every day.
afterSolved: Noodle keeps one bellyful and still beats me. I'm having a yard sale.

inhabitants.name: Doc Marrow
inhabitants.role: Giver of c2. The outpost's bone-setter, a cream terrier in light-blue scrubs. Has every part for Noodle's new vertebra, but chewed the drawing. Professional, mostly. Points the player to the Belly Scanner (c3) after c2.

default: Bone-setter. I set bones. Sometimes I chew them. Occupational hazard.
afterSolved: Identical vertebrae, stacked all the way down. Lovely spine. Not chewing it.

inhabitants.name: Penny
inhabitants.role: Giver of c4 (explain). The postmistress, a ginger bear in a post-box-red uniform, proud of her one big rubber stamp that prints a whole road at once and treats every grain alike: an LTI SSM / global convolution in a post-office cap. Fine for evenly spaced beads (Copying), smudges on scattered ones (Selective Copying). Skeptical of the 'fussy' snake. Gives f4 (convolution: her first talk after c3 checks you can read her stamp, so her 'scanner' default never shows after c3); c4 follows on the next talk.

default: Post office. My one stamp prints a whole road at once. Every grain alike. Fast!
A snake for a postman? Hmph. Come back when that scanner agrees with him.
afterSolved: My old stamp is framed now. Perfect for evenly spaced beads. Only those.

inhabitants.name: Umberto
inhabitants.role: Comic relief by the oasis water, a brown mallard: says 'um' all the time, a walking filler token (the paper's 'um' example in Section 3.5.2). Noodle used to swallow every um.

default: Um. Hi. Um. I tell Noodle stories. Um. He swallows every um.
afterSolved: Um. Noodle doesn't swallow my ums anymore. Um. Rude. Um. Fair.

challenges.title: Gulp or Let Go

spec.title: Gulp or Let Go
spec.controlsHint: ◀▶ Δ · click B, C · ⛓ link · ▶ run
spec.math: Per road, belly h = [0, 0, 0] (one channel per colour, N = 1 each). For each tile t in order: k = tokens[tile].kind; Δ = knobs[k].delta; Abar = exp(A*Δ) = exp(-Δ); Bbar = (exp(A*Δ) - 1) / A * knobs[k].B = (1 - exp(-Δ)) * knobs[k].B (zero-order hold, Eq. 4, with A = -1); h = Abar*h + Bbar*color(tile), per channel; voice y_t = knobs[k].C * h. Draw the belly as rgb(h) and the voice as rgb(y), each channel clamped to [0, 1] for display only.
judge: At every bell tile: target = colour of the most recent bead before it on the same road (every bell has one). err = max over channels |y - target|.
ok if err <= tolerance. Otherwise: silent if max|y| <= tolerance; else s = dot(y, target) / dot(target, target), r = y - s*target: faded if max|r| <= tolerance and s < 1; else mush.
At every non-bell tile: chatty if max|y| > tolerance (tag only the first such tile per road).
spec.winCondition: Every bell on all three roads is ok and no road is chatty.

solution.allWinning: Exactly 8 settings win (checked by brute force over all 8000): bead Δ=10, B=1, C=0; sand Δ=0.001, B=0 or 1, C=0; bell Δ=0.001 or 0.01, B=0 or 1, C=1. No chained (identical-column) setting can win.
solution.rule: Section 3.5.2: a large Δ resets the state and focuses on the current input (beads); a small Δ persists the state and ignores the input (sand, bells); B lets an input into the state, C lets the state out (only at bells). The rule must depend on the grain: selection, not time invariance.

challenges.design: Theme 'sand'; spec.title and spec.controlsHint come from the kit's board chrome (createBoard). LEFT: the three roads of spec.roads, one row each, left-aligned, one ≈20 px paper tile per character (spec.roadCode): beads are faceted gems in their token colour, sand is a pale dot, bells are small ink bells. Above every bell, a faint dotted ring in its target colour (the most recent bead before it on that road, as in spec.judge); no words. Each road starts with a little green paper snake head and a round belly bubble (tooltip 'A = −1'). RIGHT: the knob panel, one column per spec.kinds entry (its icon; tooltip = tip) and rows Δ, B, C (tooltips = spec.knobs[].tip). Δ: ◀ value ▶ (or the mouse wheel) through spec.knobs.delta.options. B: a 0/1 toggle drawn as a closed/open mouth. C: a 0/1 toggle drawn as a closed/open speech bubble. Above the columns, a ⛓ button (tooltip 'same for all'). Start from spec.initial. While chained, a paper chain is drawn across the three column heads and changing a knob in any column sets it in all three. Clicking ⛓ unchains (values kept; the chain falls away). Clicking it again re-chains by copying the most recently changed column to the others (the bead column if nothing changed since unchaining). Sounds: board.sfx('tick') for Δ, 'pop' for B and C, 'pin' for ⛓. A primary ▶ button (board.button) runs all three roads at once; the knobs lock during a run; ▶ again skips to the end. Each snake slides tile by tile (≈120 ms per tile). Per spec.math, its belly bubble shows h, it leaves a thin ribbon swatch of h under each tile it passes, and whenever max(y) > spec.tolerance a small speech bubble showing y pops above that tile (at a bell, inside its ring, so the two colours can be compared). Draw any colour vector v as rgb(v / max(v)) at opacity min(1, max(v)), blank when max(v) = 0: an empty belly looks blank and a weak one looks pale. After the run, spec.judge tags every bell with its spec.feedback word (✓, …, faded, mush) and puts a red 'chatty' tag on the first off-bell tile where a snake talks (at most one per road). Win (spec.winCondition): call board.solve() at once (it locks ✕ and the buttons, stamps ✓, shows spec.successText and calls api.onSolved() after its delay; the host then closes the board and plays the success lines) and wiggle the snakes meanwhile; lock the knobs. No ↩ button. Failure: board.fail('miss') (buzz, shake, a red ✕; the kit shows spec.hintAfterFailures.text once that many runs have failed). The tags stay until the next knob change. Never say which knob is wrong. Runs are unlimited; nothing resets on failure.
challenges.paperLink: Section 3.5.2 (Interpretation of Δ, B and C; Variable Spacing; Boundary Resetting); Section 3.2 and Algorithm 2 (selective versus time-invariant Δ, B, C); Theorem 1; Eq. (4); Section 3.1 and Figure 2 (Selective Copying, one bead at a time).

intro: At each bell I must say my last bead. But I gulp every grain the same. Mush!
success: Ruby! Lapis! Emerald! And not one grain of sand!
I'm so happy I could loop-de-loop! *pop* ...Ow. My back.

challenges.title: The Popped Vertebra

spec.title: The Popped Vertebra
spec.layout: Input arrow at the bottom splits into two lanes going up: the long lane (left: long1 at the bottom up to long4 at the top) and the short lane (right: short1, then short2 above it). The two lanes merge into the join slot; above it the top slot, then the output arrow. pos counts from the bottom. Every slot, the join included, looks the same, and all start empty.
spec.weightRule: Weight of one vertebra w = sum over filled slots of weights[tile], where 'E' means the current expansion value (each Linear maps D to E*D or E*D to D: E*D^2 parameters). Empty slots weigh 0. Unit: D². The left pan holds two vertebrae, so it shows 2*w.
spec.winCondition: All 8 slots hold exactly spec.solution's tiles and E === 2 (then 2 * 3E = 12 = the right pan). Exact match, no tolerance.

CENTRE: the jig, an empty vertebra-shaped frame drawn like one column of Figure 3 (spec.layout): arrows in and out, two lanes, no labels. Every slot, the join included, is the same neutral dashed rounded square: no shape hints. The lanes widen a little as E grows. BOTTOM: a tray with one stack per spec.tiles entry (unlimited copies; labels exactly spec.tiles[].label; no weights shown; 'trapezoid' = a green trapezoid, 'round' = a small circle, 'box' = a blue rounded box). Drag a tile onto any slot, or click it and then the slot (createDnd; board.sfx('paper')). Dropping on a filled slot replaces it; dragging a placed tile off the jig, or right-clicking it (preventDefault), empties the slot. RIGHT: a balance scale. Left pan: two tiny vertebra icons and the number 2·w (spec.weightRule). Right pan: Kayvee's overflowing letter cart (spec.scale.right.look) showing spec.scale.right.label and spec.scale.right.value. Unit 'D²'. The beam tilts toward the heavier pan and is level when equal, live. Under it, an E dial (◀ E ▶, tooltip 'expand') cycling spec.expansion.options from spec.expansion.initial. No ↩ button. Failure: board.fail(keys) with every key that applies, in this order: 'empty' (some slot is empty), 'bones' (some filled slot holds a wrong tile), 'tilt' (the beam is not level); the jig rattles. challenges.title: The Belly Scanner
challenges.prompt:
Two numpy functions, `float64`. A loop over time is fine.

### 1. `selective_scan(x, delta, A, B, C, h0=None)` → `(y, h_last)`
The SSM of **Eq. (2a)/(2b)**, time-varying as in **Algorithm 2**, discretized by the **ZOH of Eq. (4)**.
- `x` `(L, D)`; `delta` `(L, D)`, all > 0: one Δ per step and channel
- `A` `(D, N)`, all < 0: row `d` is the diagonal of channel `d`'s A
- `B`, `C` `(L, N)`: one row per step, shared by all channels
- `h0` `(D, N)`: the belly before step 0; `None` = zeros
- channel `d` runs its own SSM with an `N`-long state `h[d]`, using `A[d]`, `delta[t, d]`, `B[t]`, `C[t]`
- `y[t, d] = C[t] · h_t[d]` (sum over the `N` pockets)
- `y` `(L, D)`; `h_last` `(D, N)`: the state after the last step

### 2. `s6(x, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias)` → `y` `(L, D)`
Selection (**Section 3.2**, **Algorithm 2**), then `selective_scan` from a zero belly.
- `x` `(L, D)`; `A` `(D, N)`; `W_B`, `W_C` `(D, N)`; `w_delta`, `delta_bias` `(D,)`
- `B = x @ W_B`, `C = x @ W_C` (s_B, s_C = Linear_N, no bias)
- `Δ = τ_Δ(Parameter + s_Δ(x))`: Parameter = `delta_bias`; `s_Δ(x) = Broadcast_D(Linear_1(x))` with `Linear_1(x) = x @ w_delta`; τ_Δ as Section 3.2 chooses
challenges.starterCode:
import numpy as np


def selective_scan(x, delta, A, B, C, h0=None):
    """x (L, D), delta (L, D) > 0, A (D, N) < 0, B and C (L, N), h0 (D, N) or None.

    Returns (y, h_last): y (L, D), h_last (D, N).
    """
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    A = np.asarray(A, dtype=np.float64)
    L, D = x.shape
    N = A.shape[1]
    # TODO: the hourglasses are empty.
    return np.zeros((L, D)), np.zeros((D, N))


def s6(x, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias):
    """x (L, D), A (D, N), W_B and W_C (D, N), w_delta and delta_bias (D,). Returns y (L, D)."""
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    # TODO: Noodle chooses nothing yet.
    return np.zeros_like(x)
challenges.tests:
import numpy as np


def _etl_t_f64(v):
    dt = getattr(v, 'dtype', None)
    assert dt is None or dt.kind != 'f' or dt.itemsize >= 8, "float32 is too rough here: use float64"
    return np.asarray(v, dtype=np.float64)


def _etl_t_scan(*args, **kwargs):
    out = selective_scan(*args, **kwargs)
    assert isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) and len(out) == 2, "selective_scan must return a pair: (y, h_last)"
    return _etl_t_f64(out[0]), _etl_t_f64(out[1])


def _etl_t_s6(*args):
    return _etl_t_f64(s6(*args))


def _etl_t_eq(a, b, tol):
    return np.allclose(a, b, rtol=0.0, atol=tol)


def test_one_grain_by_hand():
    ln2 = np.log(2.0)
    x, delta, A, B, C = (np.array([[v]]) for v in (2.0, ln2, -1.0, 1.0, 1.0))
    y, h = _etl_t_scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    assert y.shape == (1, 1), f"L = D = 1: y must have shape (1, 1), got {y.shape}"
    assert h.shape == (1, 1), f"D = N = 1: h_last must have shape (1, 1), got {h.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "the belly is nan/inf after one friendly grain"
    if _etl_t_eq(y, [[2.0 * ln2]], 1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("A shortcut! That B̄ is only roughly right. Eq. (4) gives the exact rule.")
    if _etl_t_eq(y, [[2.0]], 1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("B went into the belly raw. Eq. (4) discretizes B too, not only A.")
    assert _etl_t_eq(y, [[1.0]], 1e-9), "one grain (x = 2, Δ = ln 2, A = -1, B = C = 1): wrong belly. See Eq. (4)."
    assert _etl_t_eq(h, [[1.0]], 1e-9), "h_last must be the state after the last step"
    y2, h2 = _etl_t_scan(x, delta, A, B, C, h0=np.array([[4.0]]))
    assert _etl_t_eq(y2, [[3.0]], 1e-9) and _etl_t_eq(h2, [[3.0]], 1e-9), (
        "with h0 = 4: wrong belly. h0 is the state *before* step 0")


def test_two_pockets_two_steps_by_hand():
    ln2 = np.log(2.0)
    x = np.array([[1.0], [3.0]])
    delta = np.array([[ln2], [ln2]])
    A = np.array([[-1.0, -2.0]])
    B = np.array([[1.0, 2.0], [0.0, 1.0]])
    C = np.array([[1.0, 1.0], [2.0, -1.0]])
    y, h = _etl_t_scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    assert y.shape == (2, 1), f"L = 2, D = 1: y must have shape (2, 1), got {y.shape}"
    assert h.shape == (1, 2), f"D = 1, N = 2: h_last must have shape (1, 2), got {h.shape}"
    if _etl_t_eq(y, [[2.0794415416798357], [-1.732867951399863]], 1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("A shortcut! That B̄ is only roughly right. Eq. (4) gives the exact rule.")
    assert _etl_t_eq(y, [[1.25], [-0.8125]], 1e-9), (
        "N = 2, two steps: wrong y. Each step has its own B_t, C_t; y_t sums the pockets.")
    assert _etl_t_eq(h, [[0.25, 1.3125]], 1e-9), "h_last must be the state after the last step"


def test_theorem_1_the_old_gate_inside():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    L, D = 12, 3
    g = rng.uniform(0.02, 0.98, size=(L, D))
    delta = -np.log1p(-g)
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    y, h = _etl_t_scan(x, delta, -np.ones((D, 1)), np.ones((L, 1)), np.ones((L, 1)))
    assert y.shape == (L, D), f"expected y of shape {(L, D)}, got {y.shape}"
    assert h.shape == (D, 1), f"expected h_last of shape {(D, 1)}, got {h.shape}"
    want = np.zeros((L, D))
    s = np.zeros(D)
    for t in range(L):
        s = (1.0 - g[t]) * s + g[t] * x[t]
        want[t] = s
    assert _etl_t_eq(y, want, 1e-10), "Theorem 1 case (N = 1, A = -1, B = C = 1): wrong belly. See Appendix C."
    assert _etl_t_eq(h[:, 0], want[-1], 1e-10), "h_last must be the state after the last step"


def test_big_step_starts_fresh():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(4)
    L, D, N = 9, 3, 4
    A = -np.tile(np.arange(1, N + 1, dtype=np.float64), (D, 1))
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.05, 0.6, size=(L, D))
    delta[5] = 60.0
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    y, _ = _etl_t_scan(x, delta, A, B, C, h0=rng.normal(size=(D, N)))
    x2 = x.copy()
    x2[:5] = rng.normal(size=(5, D)) * 3.0
    y2, _ = _etl_t_scan(x2, delta, A, B, C, h0=rng.normal(size=(D, N)))
    assert y.shape == (L, D), f"expected y of shape {(L, D)}, got {y.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "a big Δ made the belly nan/inf"
    assert not np.allclose(y[:5], y2[:5]), "before step 5, different grains (and h0) must give a different belly"
    assert _etl_t_eq(y[5:], y2[5:], 1e-9), "huge Δ at step 5: the past (and h0) must stop mattering from step 5 on"


def test_tiny_step_lets_a_grain_slide_by():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
    L, D, N = 8, 2, 3
    A = -rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0, size=(D, N))
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.1, 1.0, size=(L, D))
    delta[3] = 1e-9
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    y, _ = _etl_t_scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "a tiny Δ made the belly nan/inf"
    x2 = x.copy()
    x2[3] += 1000.0
    y2, _ = _etl_t_scan(x2, delta, A, B, C)
    assert _etl_t_eq(y, y2, 1e-4), "tiny Δ at step 3: making that grain 1000 bigger should barely matter"
    x3 = x.copy()
    x3[2] += 1.0
    y3, _ = _etl_t_scan(x3, delta, A, B, C)
    assert not np.allclose(y[4:], y3[4:]), "tiny Δ at step 3: the belly from step 2 must still be carried past it"


def test_never_peeks_down_the_road():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(6)
    L, D, N = 10, 3, 2
    A = -rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0, size=(D, N))
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.1, 1.0, size=(L, D))
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    y, _ = _etl_t_scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    x2, d2, B2, C2 = x.copy(), delta.copy(), B.copy(), C.copy()
    x2[6:] += 5.0
    d2[6:] *= 3.0
    B2[6:] -= 2.0
    C2[6:] += 1.0
    y2, _ = _etl_t_scan(x2, d2, A, B2, C2)
    assert _etl_t_eq(y[:6], y2[:6], 1e-10), "changing grains 6.. changed steps 0..5: the scanner peeked ahead"
    assert not np.allclose(y[6:], y2[6:]), "steps 6.. must notice their own changed grains"


def test_long_road_in_two_chunks():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    L, D, N = 12, 3, 4
    A = -rng.uniform(0.3, 3.0, size=(D, N))
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.05, 1.0, size=(L, D))
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    y, h = _etl_t_scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    assert y.shape == (L, D) and h.shape == (D, N), f"expected {(L, D)} and {(D, N)}, got {y.shape} and {h.shape}"
    assert np.max(np.abs(y)) > 1e-3, "the belly stays empty on a long, busy road"
    ya, ha = _etl_t_scan(x[:5], delta[:5], A, B[:5], C[:5])
    yb, hb = _etl_t_scan(x[5:], delta[5:], A, B[5:], C[5:], h0=ha)
    assert _etl_t_eq(np.concatenate([ya, yb]), y, 1e-10), "two chunks (h_last fed in as h0) must match one long scan"
    assert _etl_t_eq(hb, h, 1e-10), "after two chunks, h_last must match the long scan's h_last"


def test_belly_is_linear_in_the_grains():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(8)
    L, D, N = 7, 2, 3
    A = -rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0, size=(D, N))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.05, 1.0, size=(L, D))
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    x1 = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    x2 = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    y1, _ = _etl_t_scan(x1, delta, A, B, C)
    y2, _ = _etl_t_scan(x2, delta, A, B, C)
    y12, _ = _etl_t_scan(2.0 * x1 - 3.0 * x2, delta, A, B, C)
    assert np.max(np.abs(y1)) > 1e-3, "the belly stays empty"
    assert _etl_t_eq(y12, 2.0 * y1 - 3.0 * y2, 1e-9), "Δ, B, C held fixed: scanning 2·x1 - 3·x2 must give 2·y1 - 3·y2"


def test_a_whole_road_by_the_book():
    x = np.array([[-0.9, -0.63], [0.74, -0.71], [-0.52, -1.61], [-0.37, -1.03], [-0.64, 2.88]])
    delta = np.array([[1.14, 1.25], [0.7, 1.17], [1.08, 1.37], [1.1, 1.07], [0.4, 0.76]])
    A = np.array([[-2.64, -0.59, -2.74], [-1.77, -1.32, -1.2]])
    B = np.array([[1.28, 0.44, -0.12], [1.32, 0.0, 0.62], [-0.44, 0.3, -0.74], [-0.9, 1.11, -0.42], [2.12, 1.23, -0.93]])
    C = np.array([[1.39, -0.65, 0.53], [0.19, -1.13, -0.27], [-0.45, -0.63, -0.27], [0.78, -0.09, 0.97], [-0.49, 1.91, 0.39]])
    y, h = _etl_t_scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    assert y.shape == (5, 2) and h.shape == (2, 3), f"expected (5, 2) and (2, 3), got {y.shape} and {h.shape}"
    assert _etl_t_eq(y, [[-0.343057331522, -0.427752532804], [0.252449194484, 0.0147556825409], [0.0697493729232, -0.149690733504], [0.19729209814, 0.904597158158], [-1.01855110296, 0.973718384743]], 1e-8), (
        "L = 5, D = 2, N = 3: wrong y. Check Ā, B̄ (Eq. 4), the update, then the read-out.")
    assert _etl_t_eq(h, [[-0.291869169639, -0.641833832928, 0.164963140542], [2.67935468128, 1.43142400799, -1.14722481202]], 1e-8), "L = 5, D = 2, N = 3: wrong h_last"


def test_s6_chooses_by_the_book():
    x = np.array([[0.5, -1.0], [1.5, 0.25], [-0.75, 2.0], [0.0, -0.5]])
    A = np.array([[-1.0, -2.0], [-0.5, -3.0]])
    W_B = np.array([[0.8, -0.3], [0.2, 0.6]])
    W_C = np.array([[-0.4, 1.1], [0.7, 0.5]])
    w_delta = np.array([1.2, -0.9])
    delta_bias = np.array([-0.5, 0.3])
    y = _etl_t_s6(x, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias)
    assert y.shape == (4, 2), f"s6 must return y of shape (L, D) = (4, 2), got {y.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "s6 returned nan/inf on a small, friendly road"
    assert _etl_t_eq(y, [[-0.0744921831255, 0.236877087446], [-0.995520042995, -0.173355165481], [2.28072866683, 0.475441213599], [-0.22905220853, -0.0802864107894]], 1e-8), (
        "s6: wrong y. Check B, C and Δ = τ_Δ(Parameter + s_Δ(x)) (Section 3.2).")


def test_s6_one_choice_for_every_channel():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(9)
    L, D, N = 8, 3, 2
    A = -np.tile(np.array([1.0, 2.0]), (D, 1))
    W_B = rng.normal(size=(D, N))
    W_C = rng.normal(size=(D, N))
    w_delta = np.array([60.0, 0.0, 0.0])
    delta_bias = np.array([-1.0, -0.5, 0.0])
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    x[:, 0] = 0.0
    x[4, 0] = 1.0
    y = _etl_t_s6(x, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias)
    assert y.shape == (L, D), f"expected y of shape {(L, D)}, got {y.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "s6 returned nan/inf"
    x2 = x.copy()
    x2[:4, 1:] = rng.normal(size=(4, D - 1)) * 2.0
    y2 = _etl_t_s6(x2, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias)
    assert not np.allclose(y[:4], y2[:4]), "different grains before the marker must give a different belly"
    assert _etl_t_eq(y[4:], y2[4:], 1e-9), "a marker must reset every channel. How is s_Δ(x) built? (3.2, end of 3.5.1)"
intro: Doc Marrow's note: 'Follow Noodle grain by grain. No shortcuts.'
success: The hourglasses flip. The scanner's belly matches Noodle's.

challenges.title: The Old Stamp
challenges.question: Why can't my stamp carry scattered beads? What does Noodle do with each grain instead?
rubric: Time invariance (Section 2, 'Linear Time Invariance'). Core: the stamp is an LTI SSM / global convolution whose parameters (Δ, A, B, C) are the same at every step, so it treats every grain alike, whatever the grain is. Bonus, not required: the kernel K = (CB̄, CĀB̄, …, CĀ^k B̄, …) of Eq. (3).

Why scattered beads break it (Section 3.1, Figure 2). Core: the spacing between beads varies at random, so one fixed kernel cannot know where the beads are; what to keep has to be decided from what each grain is (its content). Bonus, not required: the evenly spaced Copying contrast (a fixed kernel solves it by tracking time alone) and Table 1 (S4 18.3% vs S6 97.0%).
Selection (Section 3.2, Algorithm 2). Core: Noodle's Δ, B and C are computed from the current grain (functions of the input), so his dynamics change from grain to grain (time-varying).

What Δ does (Section 3.5.2). Core: a large Δ resets the belly and takes in the current grain (keep the bead); a small Δ keeps the belly and ignores the current grain (let sand pass). Story words for Δ such as step or gulp count. Bonus, not required: B decides what gets into the belly, C what comes out.

The price (Sections 3.2-3.3). Core: once the parameters depend on the input the model is no longer a convolution, so the fast stamp (convolution) mode is lost and Mamba runs a (parallel) scan, still linear in length. Optional: hardware details (SRAM, kernel fusion, recomputation).
challenges.passBar: Pass if at least 3 of the 5 criteria are met and criteria 2 and 4 are both among them. Judge each criterion by its core only; parts marked bonus or optional are never required. Fail regardless of the count if the answer reverses Δ (says a large Δ ignores the grain or a small Δ resets the belly), says a fixed kernel cannot solve evenly spaced Copying either, says selective SSMs are still computed as a convolution, or credits architectural gating (multiplication) alone with handling scattered beads.
challenges.paperLink: Section 2 (Linear Time Invariance; recurrence (2) vs convolution (3)); Section 3.1 and Figure 2 (Copying vs Selective Copying); Section 4.1.1 and Table 1; Section 3.2 and Algorithm 2 (selection); Section 3.5.2 and Theorem 1 (what Δ, B, C do); Section 3.3 and Appendix D (scan instead of convolution, hardware-aware).
intro: So the fussy snake delivers. Pfft.
Evenly spaced beads? Perfect prints. Scattered beads? Smudges!
success: Oh. My stamp never looks at the grains at all. It only counts steps.
Noodle decides with every grain. Fine. The stamp goes in a nice frame.
retry: Hmm. My stamp still thinks it's perfect.
Why do scattered beads smudge? What does Noodle do with a bead? With sand?

fundamentals.title: Hidden state
intro: Noodle has ONE small belly, and the road never ends. How does it all fit?!

check.question: At grain 5, Noodle's belly is made from…

wrong: Nope! I'd know. I live on his tail.
success: Old belly plus one new grain, again and again. It never gets bigger!
known: Ooh, your book glows! It knows how Noodle's one belly holds a whole road? Aww.
fundamentals.record: A recurrent model's one small belly of memory: each step remakes it from the last state and the new input, h_t = f(h_(t-1), x_t). It never grows.

fundamentals.title: Exponential decay
intro: Noodle's ruby used to fade on the sand, grain by grain. I counted! Can you?

check.question: A glow of 1 keeps half of itself each grain. Left after 3 grains? (decimal)

wrong: Nope! I counted on both ears. Twice.
success: 0.125! An eighth. Fading, fading... but never quite zero.
known: Your book knows how a glow fades, grain by grain? Phooey. I counted for nothing.
fundamentals.record: Multiply by the same share a (0 < a < 1) each step and a^t is left after t steps; at e^(-k) a step, e^(-kt). It dwindles, and never quite dies.

fundamentals.title: Big-O cost
intro: Each new letter, I check against ALL the letters in my cart.

check.question: For n letters, my total checking grows like…

wrong: Nope. And I've checked a LOT of letters.
success: n². Twice the road, four times the checking. My poor paws!
known: Your book already knows how my checking piles up? Hmph. Back to sorting.
fundamentals.record: How the toil swells with n: one pass is O(n), doubling when n doubles; each against all is O(n²), and quadruples.

fundamentals.title: Convolution
intro: The scanner agrees? Hmph. First, prove you can read my stamp.

check.question: At each grain: 1 × this grain + 2 × the grain before. Road 0, 1, 0, 0 prints…

wrong: Hmph. Wrong. My stamp would blush.
success: Hmph. You CAN read a stamp. Now, about that snake...
known: Your book reads stamps already? Hmph. Saves ink.
fundamentals.record: One kernel, slid along the sequence: each output a weighted sum of nearby inputs, by the same weights at every position.

artefact.name: The Sifting Hourglass
artefact.description: Opens for beads, pinches shut for sand. One small bulb, only what matters.
artefact.look: A small hourglass (about 0.6 units tall): two clear glass cones meeting at a narrow neck, warm wooden caps top and bottom, a little cone of golden sand in the lower bulb. A green paper snake coils around the top cap with its head raised. Idle: it turns slowly; sand trickles, the neck pinches and the trickle stops, then a coloured bead drops through.

guard: Do not say what Δ does (a large Δ resets the state and focuses on the current input; a small Δ keeps the state and ignores it), what Δ → ∞ or Δ → 0 means, or which Δ, B or C (0 or 1) a bead, a sand grain or a bell needs.

Do not compute any power, decay, count of checks, growth rate or stamp print for numbers or roads the player brings, and never say which option of a villager's question is right. offlineHints.text: The step decides: linger, or let it pass. Section 3.5.2. Theorem 1, twice.
One letter lets in. One lets out. The last lines of 3.5.2 know which is which.
Who treats every grain alike learns nothing of grains. Section 2 names it.
Even roads, scattered roads. Figure 2 draws both. Section 3.1 says why.
Bones stack in one shape, again and again. In Figure 3, only one is a snake.
Weigh the projections, not the snake. Section 3.4 counts them in D squared.
A named rule makes the continuous discrete. Equation 4. Hold the grain.
Carry the belly one grain at a time. Eqs. 2a and 2b, a little t on every letter.
What chooses the step? Algorithm 2, line four. The end of Section 3.2 names τ.
Long roads are walked in pieces. Appendix D says what to carry between them.
A stamp needs a rule that never changes. Section 3.3 names its heir.
An old gate sleeps in the snake. Theorem 1 wakes it. Appendix C shows its bones.
The belly's making: Equation 2a. Its fading: Equation 4, then 3a. The counting is yours.
A cart that forgets nothing pays for it. Section 3.1 names the toll.
The stamp's portrait: Equation 3. Press it yourself.
